title: Opus 5.5 Release Date: Anthropic Ships Its New Flagship
summary: No official Opus 5.5 release date exists yet. Here is what Anthropic has actually confirmed and why the circulating leaks stay unverified as of September 2026.
body_markdown:
Anthropic has not announced Claude Opus 5.5, has not confirmed a release date, and has not published any official pricing, benchmark, or model card for it. Every "release date" claim circulating right now traces back to a small cluster of social media posts, not to Anthropic. If you are trying to plan around an Opus 5.5 launch, the honest answer is that no launch has been scheduled publicly, and the current flagship remains Claude Opus 5.


This piece separates what is confirmed from what is speculation, so you can make decisions on facts rather than screenshots.


## There is no official Opus 5.5 release date


No Opus 5.5 release date exists because Anthropic has never announced the model. As of September 22, 2026, there is no announcement post, no entry in the Claude Platform docs, no public API identifier, and no pricing page for anything called Opus 5.5. A release date requires a source that can set one, and the only party that can do that here is Anthropic.


The claims you may have seen point to a Tuesday launch, sometimes widened to "Monday or Tuesday." That wobble is a useful tell. A confirmed date does not drift by a day depending on which account you read.


## Where the Opus 5.5 rumors come from


The rumors come from roughly 10 posts by 7 authors over about 8 hours, none of them from Anthropic. The most careful third-party write-up of the episode counts zero posts marked as evidence in the whole set. That is the entire foundation for the "release date," the pricing sheet, and the benchmark boasts making the rounds.


Several details inside the rumor set contradict each other, which matters more than the volume of posts:


- Two different internal codenames circulate, "claude-wafer-cap" and "claude-wafer-eap," with no way to confirm either is real.
- One post claimed a working checkpoint already existed, but supplied no model output, evaluation log, or reproducible test.
- A widely shared 3D demo was reportedly pulled after the footage was traced to an unrelated video uploaded days earlier.


A demo that gets retracted is not a capability. It is a reminder to ask for the prompt, the model identifier, the timestamp, and an independent reproduction before believing any screenshot.


*Table 1: Confirmed facts versus circulating claims, as of September 2026*


**Detail** **Status** **Source**


Opus 5.5 exists as a product Unconfirmed No Anthropic announcement


Release date (reported "Tuesday") Unconfirmed rumor Social posts, self-contradicting


Pricing ("$4 input / $20 output") Unconfirmed rumor Unofficial screenshot


Context window ("872K tokens") Unconfirmed rumor Third-party repost


Benchmark wins over GPT-6 Unconfirmed opinion No test data


Opus 5 is the current flagship Confirmed Anthropic, July 24, 2026


## What Anthropic has actually shipped


The confirmed Claude lineup as of late September 2026 does not include an Opus point-release above 5. Anthropic's public models are the ones with announcement posts and documentation behind them, and that is the correct reference point for any planning decision.


Claude Opus 5 launched on July 24, 2026 as the flagship. Anthropic describes it as a proactive model that approaches the frontier intelligence of Claude Fable 5 at half the price, and it became the default model on Claude Max at release. It carries the model string claude-opus-5, a 1-million-token context window, and standard API pricing of 5 dollars per million input tokens and 25 dollars per million output tokens.


Claude Sonnet 5 arrived earlier, on June 30, 2026, priced at 2 dollars per million input tokens and 10 dollars per million output tokens. It is the default model on the Free and Pro plans. Below it sits Haiku 4.5, the fastest and cheapest option. Above Opus sits Anthropic's Mythos tier, whose public member is[Fable 5.1](https://emergent.sh/learn/claude-fable-5-1-benchmarks) .


The version before the current flagship, Opus 4.8, also still exists and now serves as an automatic fallback when a safety classifier flags an[Opus 5](https://emergent.sh/learn/what-is-claude-opus-5) request. None of these is Opus 5.5.


## Why a jump straight to "5.5" would be unusual


Skipping from Opus 5 to Opus 5.5 would break the cadence Anthropic has actually followed, which is part of why the naming claim deserves scrutiny. Recent Opus releases moved in fine-grained steps,[Opus 4.6 to 4.7](https://emergent.sh/learn/claude-opus-4-7-vs-opus-4-6) to 4.8 to 5. A leap to 5.5 as the very next release implies a larger revision than that pattern suggests, and the rumor set offers no evidence to explain the jump.


There is a simpler reading. Version numbers shape expectations before anyone runs a single test, so a bold number attached to an unverified leak is exactly the kind of claim that spreads fast and confirms nothing.


## How to evaluate the next Opus release


Wait for four concrete signals before treating any Opus 5.5 report as real, because each one is something only Anthropic can produce. A model card settles the name, context window, and supported features. A public API identifier separates a shipping model from an internal experiment. A pricing page confirms or kills the rumored numbers. An announcement post ties it all to a real date.


Until those appear, the safe move for anyone building on Claude is to keep planning against Opus 5, which is documented, priced, and available today. That stability matters most when you are prototyping an app and need a model you can count on. You can start building on[Emergent](https://emergent.sh/) with the[Universal LLM Key](https://help.emergent.sh/universal-key) , which gives single-credential access with unified billing across supported Claude, GPT, and Gemini models.


When Anthropic does announce the next Opus, the facts will come from its own newsroom and docs, not from a screenshot. That is the difference between a release and a rumor.
